newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Feb electric futures expire lower, Mar flat.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Feb electric futures expire lower, Mar flat.

text.p: NYMEX February electricity futures expired lower Tuesday amid weaker cash power prices and natural gas futures, and outlook of mild weather in the western half of the U.S.
"The weather is going to be warmer. There's still a lot of water," said an East Coast paper broker, referring to ample hydroelectric supplies in the West.
February California-Oregon Border (COB) futures expired down 18 cents at $13.55 a megawatt hour (MWh) after trading in a 35 cent range.
March COB settled down three cents at $11.40. Active deferred COB contracts finished five to 20 cents lower.
February Palo Verde (PV) futures expired 53 cents at $15.29/MWh after moving between $15.25 and $15.50. March PV settled unchanged $13.60.

Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) returned to the daily, peak power market today after an absence of nearly a week and offered offered up to 200 MW of firm power for Wednesday at $14.00/MWh for Northwest deliveries and $15.00 for COB sales, slightly below than Monday's spot ranges.
Day-ahead peak power prices at COB and PV fell $1.00-$1.50 from Monday's levels after BPA resume peak, day-ahead sales.

NYMEX March Henry Hub natgas futures settled down 6.9 cents at $2.546 per million British thermal units. February gas deliveries to the San Juan Hub in New Mexico were pegged at $2.42-$2.46, down from Monday's $2.45-$2.50.
Temperatures through the Pacific Northwest were expected to average five to 10 degrees Fahrenheit above normal through the week with rain expected also through the week and into the weekend.
In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to be five to 10 degrees above average this week but were called to rise to 10 to 15 degrees above normal in the eastern areas later in the week.

Separately, outage at a 500 kilovolt transmission line, which runs from Snohomish County, Wash. to the Canadian border, is expected to re-energize later this week after damage from an ice storm more than a week ago.
A 262 megawatt coal-fired unit at the Rawhide power plant in northern Colorado is expected resume operation Wednesday after being shut last Saturday for boiler tube repairs.
NYMEX estimated 303 COB and 260 PV contracts were sold.
